correctness.rationale: Every nonselected edge must have precisely one selected neighboring edge, while a selected edge is unrestricted. This produces the four-state pair transfer M and terminal vector h. Direct exact arithmetic verifies M⁴=M³+M and M³h=M²h+h. The transfer formula correctly accounts for each of the three edges at the trivalent root, including triangle c=3. It yields commuting recurrences F(c,t)=F(c−1,t)+F(c−3,t) for c>=6 and F(c,t)=F(c,t−1)+F(c,t−3) for t>=4, with initial rows (3,3,6),(4,5,8),(6,9,12). The cycle trace tr(M^{c+t}) obeys the same recursion and the 3x3 differences are strictly positive; double induction proves strict comparison everywhere. Separately written edge-subset brute force c+t<=13 matches every parameter, and exact arithmetic checks recurrence and inequality on c,t<10. Neither bounded check is the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: Grippo–Lin–Moyano–Vera's July 2026 full 30-page primary preprint was directly inspected: Conjecture 5.1 is the connected-graph cycle bound, Theorem 5.2 is its cycle recurrence, and sections 3–4 give other extremal classes and generic generalized-series-parallel counting algorithms. It does not state a lollipop bivariate closed form or its strict cycle comparison; a procedure to count one given graph is not itself a theorem comparing all (c,t). Their 2025 predecessor covers different algorithmic restrictions. No directly covering published mathematical record was found under equivalent names (unicyclic cycle-with-tail, tadpole graph).
residual_risks: A different title under tadpole/unicyclic PED-set counting could contain an equivalent pre-existing generating function.
The published 2026 generic counting algorithm is strong methodological antecedent, but does not itself assert the strict all-lollipop inequality.
No conclusion for arbitrary unicyclic graphs or all connected graphs.

value.rationale: Strictly proves a concrete infinite two-parameter connected-unicyclic subclass of an explicit open extremal conjecture, and classifies all counts through an exact rational generating function. The parameter ranges include arbitrarily long cycles and tails, so not an arbitrary tiny finite slice. It does not settle the conjecture for general connected graphs.

limitations: Lollipop graphs only, c>=3 and t>=1.
PED permits adjacent selected edges; confusing with efficient edge domination changes counts.
Finite brute checks are not the proof of global inequalities.
